current_content_summary: The user-facing real-number theory, built on CoreReal. Re-exposes <, <=, +, unary -, *, inv, %r (from_int), binary - and / , plus > and >= (display-only abbrevs), as well as `|_|` (absolute value) and b2r (bool-to-{0.0,1.0}). Bridges to Int via fromintN/fromintD/fromintM/eq_fromint/le_fromint/lt_fromint. Clones Ring.Field (see the future Ring.ec entry) at type real under the name RField, giving real the full ring/field API (with ofintR and intmulr connecting it back to plain integer arithmetic, and double_half as a named convenience lemma) -- RField is then imported so `^` resolves to RField.exp. Defines the completeness axioms for real numbers via lub/has_lub/lub_upper_bound/lub_adherent, and intp (an integer-part operator via choiceb) leading to floor/ceil (with floor_bound as the defining axiom, and ceil derived from floor) and their standard lemmas (floor_le/ceil_ge, floor_mono, isint, ceil_eqP/floor_eqP). Also registers `ring`/`field` tactic instances for real (`instance ring with real ...` / `instance field with real ...`), which is what actually lets the `ring`/`field` tactics work on real-number goals. Ends with a block of lemmas explicitly commented '(* WARNING Lemmas used by tactics: *)' -- upto2_abs, upto2_notbad, upto2_imp_bad, upto_bad_false/or/sub, eq_upto, upto_abs, upto_le -- which are the generic real-analysis lemmas underlying EasyCrypt's 'reasoning up to a bad event' proof pattern (used e.g. by PROM's collision-bound machinery).
